types.summary: MapEntity in Hammer is a type of `MapNode` that has a set of key/value pairs. The keyvalues represent the authoritative state of the entity. types.name: BeamEffect
types.summary: The BeamEffect component creates a visual beam effect in the scene, simulating a continuous line or laser-like effect. Unlike LineRenderer these beams can change over time, spawn multiple instances, and have various properties like color, texture, and lifetime. This is a useful component for creating things like laser beams, energy effects and tracers.

members.name: SpawnBeam
members.summary: Spawns a new beam and adds it to the effect.

members.summary: Thickness of the beam in world units. Controls how wide the beam appears.

members.summary: World position the beam targets if no target object is set. Used as the endpoint for the beam.

members.summary: GameObject to target with the beam. If assigned, overrides TargetPosition and uses the object's world position as the endpoint.

members.name: TargetRandom
members.summary: Random offset applied to the target position for visual variation. Adds randomness to the endpoint.

members.name: FollowPoints
members.summary: If true, the beam endpoints follow their source and target positions each frame, updating dynamically.

members.name: BeamsPerSecond
members.summary: Number of beams spawned per second. Controls the spawn rate for continuous effects.

members.name: MaxBeams
members.summary: Maximum number of beams that can exist at once. Limits the total active beams.

members.name: InitialBurst
members.summary: Number of beams spawned immediately when the effect is enabled.

members.name: BeamLifetime
members.summary: Lifetime of each beam in seconds. Determines how long a beam remains before being removed or respawned.

members.name: Looped
members.summary: If true, beams respawn automatically when they expire, creating a looping effect.

members.name: Texture
members.summary: Texture applied to the beam. Defines the visual appearance along the beam's length.

members.name: Material
members.summary: Material applied to the beam. Defines the visual appearance along the beam's length. The material should be based on the `line.shader`.

members.name: TextureOffset
members.summary: Offset of the texture along the beam. Shifts the texture start position.

members.name: TextureScale
members.summary: Scale of the texture along the beam. Controls how many world units each texture tile covers.

members.name: TextureScrollSpeed
members.summary: Speed at which the texture scrolls along the beam. Positive values scroll in one direction, negative in the other.

members.name: TextureScroll
members.summary: This is pretty much the same as TextureOffset - but it's seperate so you can use offset for offset, and scroll to scroll.

members.name: FilterMode
members.summary: Controls texture filtering on this beam effect.

members.name: BeamColor
members.summary: Color gradient of the beam over its lifetime. Defines how the color changes from birth to death.

members.name: Alpha
members.summary: Alpha multiplier for the beam's color. Controls transparency over the beam's lifetime.

members.name: Brightness
members.summary: Brightness multiplier for the beam's color. Adjusts intensity over the beam's lifetime.

members.name: Additive
members.summary: If true, the beam is rendered additively, making it appear to glow.

members.name: Shadows
members.summary: If true, the beam casts shadows in the scene.

members.summary: If true, the beam is affected by scene lighting.

members.summary: If true, the beam is rendered as opaque rather than transparent.

members.summary: Amount of feathering applied to the beam's depth, softening its intersection with geometry.

members.summary: If true, the beam visually travels from start to end, useful for tracer effects.

types.summary: The Decal component projects textures onto model's opaque or transparent surfaces. They inherit and modify the PBR properties of the surface they're projected on.

members.summary: How long should this decal live for?

members.summary: If true then the decal will repeat itself forever

members.name: Transient
members.summary: If true then this decal will automatically get removed when maxdecals are exceeded. This is good for things like bullect impacts, where you want to keep them around for as long as possible but also don't want to have an unlimited amount of them hanging around. Note that while the component will be destroyed, you probably want a TemporaryEffect component on the GameObject to make sure it all gets fully deleted.

types.summary: A GPU data buffer intended for use with a `ComputeShader`. You can read and write arbitrary data to and from the CPU and GPU. types.name: NavMeshAgent
types.summary: An agent that can navigate the navmesh defined in the scene.

members.name: SetAgentPosition
members.summary: If you want to move the agent from one position to another

members.name: MoveTo
members.summary: Navigate to the position

members.name: SetPath
members.summary: Assigns a precalculated path for the agent to follow. The agent will attempt to follow the path, but may adjust its movement to avoid obstacles or other agents. If the path becomes invalid during navigation, it may be recalculated completely.

members.name: GetPath
members.summary: Returns the agent's current path as a NavMeshPath. This is not free, so avoid calling it every frame.

members.name: Stop
members.summary: Stop moving, or whatever we're doing

members.name: CompleteLinkTraversal
members.summary: Finish link traversal, must be called after traversing a link if AutoTraverseLinks is false.

members.name: GetLookAhead
members.summary: Get a point on the current path, distance away from here. This is a simplified path so only includes the first few corners.

members.name: Acceleration
members.summary: The maximum acceleration a agent can have. This is how fast the agent can change its velocity. If you want snappy movement this should be as high or higher than `MaxSpeed`.

members.name: UpdatePosition
members.summary: Set the Position of the GameObject to the agent position every frame. You can turn this off and handle it yourself by using the AgentPosition property.

members.name: UpdateRotation
members.summary: This will simply face the direction it is moving. It is not configurable on purpose, so you should really turn this off and be doing this yourself if you need it to do anything specific.

members.name: AllowedAreas
members.summary: What areas the agent is allowed to travel on. If empty, all areas are allowed.

members.name: ForbiddenAreas
members.summary: What areas the agent is not allowed to travel on. If empty, no areas are forbidden.

members.name: AllowDefaultArea
members.summary: Is the agent allowed to travel on the default area?

members.name: AutoTraverseLinks
members.summary: Should the agent automatically traverse links when it reaches them? Or do you want to implement your own link traversal logic?

members.name: Separation
members.summary: Gets or sets the separation factor used to control how strongly agents avoid crowding each other.

members.name: AgentPosition
members.summary: Updated with the agent's position, even if UpdatePosition is false

members.name: TargetPosition
members.summary: Gets the current target position for the agent, if one is set.

members.name: WishVelocity
members.summary: The velocity the agent would like to move at, you can pass this into a PlayerController.

members.name: IsNavigating
members.summary: Returns true if the agent is currently navigating to a target.

members.name: LinkEnter
members.summary: Emitted when the agent enters a link.

members.name: LinkExit
members.summary: Emitted when the agent exits a link.

members.name: IsTraversingLink
members.summary: Returns true if the agent is currently traversing a link.

members.name: Unreliable
members.summary: Message will be sent unreliably. It may not arrive and it may be received out of order. But chances are that it will arrive on time and everything will be fine. This is good for sending position updates, or spawning effects. This is the fastest way to send a message. It is also the cheapest.

members.name: Reliable
members.summary: Message will be sent reliably. Multiple attempts will be made until the recipient has received it. Use this for things like chat messages, or important events. This is the slowest way to send a message. It is also the most expensive.

members.name: SendImmediate
members.summary: Message will not be grouped up with other messages, and will be sent immediately. This is most useful for things like streaming voice data, where packets need to stream in real-time, rather than arriving with a bunch of other packets.

members.name: DiscardOnDelay
members.summary: Message will be dropped if it can't be sent quickly. Only applicable to unreliable messages.

members.summary: Only the owner may call this action

members.name: UnreliableNoDelay
members.summary: Message will be sent unreliably, not grouped up with other messages and will be dropped if it can't be sent quickly.

members.name: SubSteps
members.summary: If you're seeing objects go through other objects or you have a low tickrate, you might want to increase the number of physics substeps. This breaks physics steps down into this many substeps. The default is 1 and works pretty good. Be aware that the number of physics ticks per second is going to be tickrate * substeps. So if you're ticking at 90 and you have SubSteps set to 1000 then you're going to do 90,000 steps per second. So be careful here.

members.summary: Enable enhanced continuous collision detection (CCD) for this body. When enabled, the body performs CCD against dynamic bodies (but not against other bodies with enhanced CCD enabled). This is useful for fast-moving objects like bullets or rockets that need reliable collision detection.

types.name: MovieRecorder
types.summary: Records properties in a scene to tracks ready for use in a `MoviePlayer`. You can use this for in-game demo recording of a whole scene, or only specific properties, configured using `MovieRecorderOptions`. You can manually call `MovieTime)` to move the recording time along, then `Capture` to write all recorded properties to tracks. Alternatively, call `Start` to automatically advance and capture every fixed update, and `Stop` to finish recording. Convert the recording to a `MovieClip` by calling `ToClip`. This clip can then be played back immediately, or serialized to later use.

members.summary: If false, then instead of operating physics, and UpdateFixed in a fixed update frequency they will be called the same as Update - every frame, with a variable time delta.

members.name: SubSteps
members.summary: If you're seeing objects go through other objects or you have a low tickrate, you might want to increase the number of physics substeps. This breaks physics steps down into this many substeps. The default is 1 and works pretty good. Be aware that the number of physics ticks per second is going to be tickrate * substeps. So if you're ticking at 90 and you have SubSteps set to 1000 then you're going to do 90,000 steps per second. So be careful here.

members.name: MaxFixedUpdates
members.summary: If the frame took longer than a FixedUpdate step, we need to run multiple steps for that frame, to catch up. How many are allowed? Too few, and the simluation will run slower than the game. If you allow an unlimited amount then the frame time could snowball to infinity and never catch up.

types.name: SamplerState
types.summary: Represents a sampler state used to control how textures are sampled in shaders. Example usage: SamplerState mySampler < Attribute("sampler"); >; C# binding: var sampler = new SamplerState { Filter = FilterMode.Trilinear, AddressModeU = TextureAddressMode.Wrap, AddressModeV = TextureAddressMode.Wrap, AddressModeW = TextureAddressMode.Clamp, MaxAnisotropy = 4 }; Graphics.Attributes.Set("sampler", sampler);

members.name: Filter
members.summary: The texture filtering mode used for sampling (e.g., point, bilinear, trilinear).

members.name: AddressModeU
members.summary: The addressing mode used for the U (X) texture coordinate.

members.name: AddressModeV
members.summary: The addressing mode used for the V texture coordinate.

members.name: AddressModeW
members.summary: The addressing mode used for the W texture coordinate.

members.name: MipLodBias
members.summary: The bias applied to the calculated mip level during texture sampling. Positive values make textures appear blurrier; negative values sharpen.

members.name: MaxAnisotropy
members.summary: The maximum anisotropy level used for anisotropic filtering. Higher values improve texture quality at oblique viewing angles.

members.name: BorderColor
members.summary: Border color to use if `Border` is specified for AddressU, AddressV, or AddressW.

types.name: TextureAddressMode
types.summary: Specifies how texture coordinates outside the [0.0, 1.0] range are handled.

members.name: Wrap
members.summary: Wraps the texture coordinates. Values beyond 1.0 wrap around to the beginning. Produces a repeating tiling pattern.

members.name: Mirror
members.summary: Mirrors the texture coordinates when sampling outside the [0.0, 1.0] range. Creates a mirrored tiling effect.

members.name: Clamp
members.summary: Clamps the texture coordinates to the [0.0, 1.0] range. Texture edges are stretched when sampling outside the range.

members.name: Border
members.summary: Uses a constant border color when sampling outside the [0.0, 1.0] range. Requires a border color to be defined.

members.name: MirrorOnce
members.summary: Mirrors the texture once, then clamps to the edge. Coordinates in [0.0, 1.0] sample normally, [-1.0, 0.0] mirror once, and everything else clamps.

types.name: EmbeddedResource
types.summary: A JSON definition of an embedded resource. This is a resource that can be either standalone (in a .vtex file) or embedded in a GameResource's Json data. When it's detected in a GameResource we will create the named compiler and create the resource. When compiling the GameResource this can optionally create a compiled version of the resource on disk. When we compile a regular resource that contains this $compiler structure, it operates like any other compile, except it's totally managed by c# instead of resourcecompiler.

types.summary: Load images from disk and convert them to textures

members.name: FilePath
members.summary: The path to the image file, relative to any other assets in the project.

members.name: MaxSize
members.summary: The maximum size of the image in pixels. If the imported image is larger than this (after cropping), it will be downscaled to fit.

members.name: ConvertHeightToNormals
members.summary: When enabled, the output texture will be a normal map generated from the heightmap of the image.

members.name: NormalScale
members.summary: The scale of the normal map when using `ConvertHeightToNormals`. If negative, the normal map will be inverted.

members.name: Rotate
members.summary: How much to rotate the image by, in degrees. This is applied after cropping and padding.

members.name: FlipVertical
members.summary: Whether or not to flip the image vertically. This is done after everything else has been applied.

members.name: FlipHorizontal
members.summary: Whether or not to flip the image horizontally. This is done after everything else has been applied.

members.name: Cropping
members.summary: How many pixels from each edge to crop from the image. If negative values are used, the image will be expanded instead of cropped.

members.name: Padding
members.summary: How many pixels of padding from each edge. After the image has been cropped, padding is added without affecting the size of the image (scaling the original image down to fit padded margins).

members.name: InvertColor
members.summary: Whether or not to invert the colors of the image.

members.name: Tint
members.summary: The color the image should be tinted. This effectively multiplies the color of each pixel by this color (including alpha).

members.name: Blur
members.summary: The intensity of the blur effect. If 0, no blur is applied.

members.name: Sharpen
members.summary: The intensity of the sharpen effect. If 0, no sharpening is applied.

members.name: Brightness
members.summary: The brightness of the image.

members.name: Contrast
members.summary: The contrast of the image.

members.name: Saturation
members.summary: The saturation of the image.

members.name: Hue
members.summary: How much to adjust the hue of the image, in degrees. If 0, no hue adjustment is applied.

members.name: Colorize
members.summary: When enabled, every pixel in the image will be re-colored to the `TargetColor` (interpolated by the alpha).

members.name: TargetColor
members.summary: When `Colorize` is enabled, this is the target color that every pixel in the image will be re-colored to.

types.summary: VR overlays draw over the top of the 3D scene, they will not be affected by lighting, post processing effects or anything else in the world. This makes them ideal for HUDs or menus, or anything else that should be local to the HMD or tracked devices.If you need something in the world, consider using WorldPanel and WorldInput instead.
